name: PagerDuty
summary: PagerDuty publishes incident management plans with on-call, escalation, integrations and mobile response. Feature availability varies by plan.
focus: Evaluate ownership of deployment and operational data alongside the managed service, plan features and support you need.

name: incident.io
summary: incident.io lists Slack and Microsoft Teams incident response, on-call and status pages. Paid response plans and on-call add-ons vary by tier.
focus: Evaluate the collaboration workflow, plan scope and identity requirements alongside your need to operate the platform yourself.

name: Opsgenie
summary: Atlassian states that new Opsgenie sales ended on June 4, 2025 and support ends on April 5, 2027. Existing customers should plan a migration before that date.
focus: Inventory services, routing, schedules and escalation policies. Rebuild and test them in the destination before switching production alerts.

name: Grafana Cloud IRM
summary: Grafana documents that OnCall OSS was archived on March 24, 2026. Active development continues in Grafana Cloud IRM. The archived OSS project and Cloud IRM are different deployment choices.
focus: Choose between operating a self-hosted platform and using Grafana Cloud IRM. Check the current IRM plan and integration requirements directly.

name: Squadcast / SolarWinds Incident Response
summary: The Squadcast pricing URL now leads to SolarWinds Incident Response. Its plans list schedules, escalations, SMS and voice notifications, postmortems and mobile apps, with features varying by tier.
focus: Compare your response workflow and provider requirements, then assess the effort of operating your own deployment.

name: Splunk On-Call
summary: Splunk describes on-call scheduling, escalation policies, incident context, response reports and iOS and Android apps. Confirm commercial terms directly with the vendor.
focus: Compare scheduling, reporting and mobile workflows with OpsKnight’s installable PWA and self-hosted operational model.
